'''NEAR''' is a public [[blockchain]] platform that uses a [[Proof of stake|proof-of-stake]] consensus mechanism and provides [[Smart contract|smart-contract]] functionality. Its native [[cryptocurrency]] is NEAR. It was founded in 2018 by Illia Polosukhin and Alexander Skidanov, with mainnet launching in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tarasov |first=Katie |date=2024-06-27 |title=AI pioneer Illia Polosukhin, one of Google's 'Transformer 8,' wants to democratize artificial intelligence |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2024/06/27/illiapolosukhinai240624tarasovsf.html |access-date=2026-01-13 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref> 

NEAR was designed with a [[Shard (database architecture)|sharded]] architecture for decentralized applications and high-throughput transactions, intended to serve as an alternative to [[Ethereum]] and other [[Layer-1 blockchain|layer-one blockchain networks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NEAR Protocol: Self-Sovereignty in the Age of AI - Case - Faculty & Research - Harvard Business School |url=https://www.hbs.edu/faculty/Pages/item.aspx?num=67086 |access-date=2025-10-13 |website=www.hbs.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Solana, BNB, and the Blockchain Landscape: Ethereum vs. Competitors |url=https://www.hord.fi/blog/ethereum-vs-competitors |access-date=2025-10-08 |website=www.hord.fi |language=en}}</ref>

== History ==

=== Origins and founding (2017–2018) ===

NEAR Protocol was founded in early 2017 by Illia Polosukhin and Alexander Skidanov. Initially, the project was established as Near.ai, an [[artificial intelligence]] startup focused on [[program synthesis]]. Polosukhin was a former engineering manager at [[Google Research]], where he co-authored the 2017 paper "[[Attention Is All You Need]]," which introduced the [[Transformer (deep learning architecture)|transformer architecture]]. Skidanov was previously the director of engineering at [[SingleStore|MemSQL]] and a software engineer at [[Microsoft]].{{Citation needed|date=April 2026}}

=== Mainnet launch and funding (2019–2021) ===
The project began development on its [[shard (database architecture)|sharded]] architecture in late 2018. In July 2019, NEAR raised $12.1 million in a [[funding round]] led by Metastable Capital and Accomplice.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Daniel |first1=Kuhn |title=Dapp Platform Near Raises $12.1 Million From Metastable, Accomplice |url=https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2019/07/10/dapp-platform-near-raises-121-million-from-metastable-accomplice |website=CoinDesk |access-date=20 March 2026}}</ref>

The NEAR [[mainnet]] launched in April 2020, initially operating in a "restricted" [[proof of authority]] mode to ensure stability. In May 2020, the project closed a $21.6 million funding round led by [[Andreessen Horowitz]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Butcher |first1=Mike |title=NEAR Protocol raises $21.6M from A16Z and launches its MainNet, beating Ethereum 2.0 |url=https://techcrunch.com/2020/05/04/near-protocol-raises-21-6m-from-a16z-and-launches-its-mainnet-beating-ethereum-2-0/ |website=TechCrunch |access-date=20 March 2026}}</ref>
== Criticism and controversies ==
In 2022, Skyward Finance, an IDO/launchpad built on NEAR blockchain, was exploited for roughly $3 million after an attacker abused a flaw in the project’s treasury redemption contract. The bug, identified by security firm BlockSec, failed to check for duplicate token account IDs, enabling the attacker to redeem wrapped NEAR in a loop within a single transaction. Skyward acknowledged that its treasury had been drained and advised users to cease interacting with the contracts, noting that the incident rendered the SKYWARD token effectively worthless.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Skyward Finance suffers $3 million exploit on Near Protocol |url=https://www.theblock.co/post/182495/skyward-finance-exploit-near-protocol |access-date=2025-10-13 |website=The Block |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Makarov |first=Andrew |date=2022-11-03 |title=Skyward Finance была взломана на $3 млн. Курс нативного токена платформы упал на 94% |url=https://incrypted.com/skyward-finance-was-hacked/ |access-date=2025-10-13 |website=INCRYPTED |language=ru-RU}}</ref>

In 2023, a blockchain analyst questioned validator decentralization on [[Avalanche (blockchain platform)|Avalanche]], [[Solana (blockchain platform)|Solana]], NEAR, and other blockchain platforms. A Messari study found that roughly 35% of NEAR’s staked tokens were hosted on [[Amazon Web Services]], yielding a hosting “operational Nakamoto coefficient” of 1 (i.e., more than one-third of stake concentrated on a single provider). The report also observed geographic concentration of validators and stake in the [[United States]] and [[Germany]], limited presence in underrepresented regions, and reliance on a single [[validator]] client at the time; taken together, NEAR’s aggregated operational [[Satoshi Nakamoto|Nakamoto]] coefficient was estimated at ~1.3, indicating elevated susceptibility to correlated infrastructure or jurisdictional failures relative to a more distributed network.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dunbar |first=Stephanie |date=1 June 2023 |title=Evaluating Validator Decentralization: Geographic and Infrastructure Distribution in Proof-of-Stake Networks |url=https://messari.io/report/evaluating-validator-decentralization-geographic-and-infrastructure-distribution-in-proof-of-stake-networks |website=Messari}}</ref>

In 2024, NEAR blockchain drew criticism after its official [[Twitter|X]] (formerly Twitter) account abruptly changed its display name to “it’s all a lie” and posted anti-[[Cryptocurrency|crypto]] messages that prompted widespread speculation the account had been hacked. NEAR later indicated the episode was a marketing tactic tied to an upcoming event, which industry commentators and developers criticized as tone-deaf given the prevalence of genuine security breaches in the sector; some argued the stunt risked harming the project’s credibility. During the period of the campaign, [[Bloomberg News|''Bloomberg'']] reported that NEAR’s token declined by roughly 15% over the preceding week. ''Bloomberg'' also said that the controversy followed a real security incident in May 2023, when a compromised moderator account on NEAR’s [[Discord]] was used to promote a fraudulent airdrop.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Nicolle |first=Emily |date=2024-09-05 |title=NEAR Blockchain’s Fake-Hack Marketing Ploy Hits a Sour Note |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/newsletters/2024-09-05/near-blockchain-s-fake-hack-marketing-ploy-hits-a-sour-note |access-date=2025-10-13 |work=Bloomberg.com |language=en}}</ref>
